title: 3.0 GUI: Settings, service and phone
note: The 3.0 GUI, part 5: settings, the service and the phone. Rows 6 and 7 of HIVEM1ND 3.0. The sample is invented.

screens.title: 6.1 Settings, the phone link and the service: Settings

kids.name: text
kids.value: Each preview is drawn in the look's own palette; a choice applies at once.

kids.name: text
kids.value: See, chat and approve from your phone while it is on the same network. Access closes after 12 hours.

kids.name: text
kids.value: Sync your preferences on any device, phones included, through the same service as Nebula+.

screens.title: 6.2 Settings, the phone link and the service: Agents

kids.name: text
kids.value: The command line is how HIVEM1ND runs your units: it opens a session for each task and closes it. Auto loads the M1ND rules in every session; On demand only when a HIVEM1ND command runs.

kids.name: text
kids.value: The desktop app is separate and optional: connecting it lets you write to an agent in its own window, and the M1ND wakes it when a message arrives.

kids.name: text
kids.value: A unit can also be run by hand in an agent's app with its command, for example /executor shop. It joins the M1ND, keeps its place in the hierarchy and shows on the Map like any other.

screens.title: 6.3 Settings, the phone link and the service: Connect an agent

kids.name: text
kids.value: HIVEM1ND needs these changes on DESKTOP. Nothing is written until you apply them; Copy changes gives them to make by hand.

replies.author: User
replies.text: Ofrecer conectar los editors que se puedan tipo Claude app, Codex, Cursor, como hacemos nosotros ahora. Pero enfocarse principalmente en el CLI. Es el más accesible la verdad. Pensalo por acá y dame tus opiniones

replies.author: User
replies.text: Digo porque Cursor tuvo problemas, se puede hacer un CLI tipo chat y que se abra y descarten? También tener el flow que tenemos ahora manual de escribir en la app pero que enfoque a la orquestación eficiente de agentes via CLI que es lo más eficiente. Considerar cuestiones de permisos. pedir cambios y ofrecer hacerlos automático si se admite.

replies.author: overmind-hivem1nd
replies.text: Done as chosen in chat. 6.2 shows each agent with its CLI first (it runs the units, Auto or On demand) and the app connection as optional. 6.3 lists every configuration change before it is made, with Apply or Copy changes. 2.13 Start a session runs an Executor as one task that closes by default, or as a chat that can open other CLIs itself. Builders are gone from the sample.

replies.author: User
replies.text: Considerar potenciales fricciones, errores. Audit with Sonnet 5.5 (yours, not Cursor's).

replies.author: overmind-hivem1nd
replies.text: Done. A Sonnet 5.5 audit found 21 points. The consistency errors are fixed (aliases, counts, waiting badges, the offline LAPTOP, labels). With the owner's yes the board now also covers: agent permissions (6.3 review of every write, git apart and unticked, 6.5 Permissions with Revoke), the phone (no standing approvals on it, 7.3 lock, access open in 6.1), migration and a second machine (1.3 join, 1.4 close 2.x), deletions with confirmation and Undo (2.10, 2.18, 5.3, 6.7), failures (1.6, 1.9, 5.5, Stop in 3.3, 3.4 approval to open a CLI, Not confirmed in 3.6), the machine selector (6.4), projects in the library (4.3, 4.5), History (4.14) and accessibility (shapes for status, 32 px targets, muted text contrast). 83 screens.

replies.author: User
replies.text: No entiendo esto. Connect app es CLI?

replies.author: overmind-hivem1nd
replies.text: No: they are two different connections, and 6.2 now says so. The left column is the command line (CLI), how HIVEM1ND runs the units, a session per task. The right column is the desktop app (Claude app, Codex app, Cursor editor), optional, for writing to an agent in its own window; its button names the app.
